You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.

You will give feedback to a variable with the following role: <ROLE> a chosen response to a user query </ROLE>. Here is an evaluation of the variable using a language model:

<LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT> You are a language model tasked with evaluating a chosen response by comparing it with a rejected response to a user query. Analyze the strengths and weaknesses of each response, step by step, and explain why one is chosen or rejected.

**User Query**:
I want to open the developler tools in chrome with ctrl + shift + i on this website: https://mnsw.pro/
It doesnt work. works on other websites. even here. what is wrong?

**Rejected Response**:
I don't see a problem with this website. It is working fine.

**Do NOT generate a response to the query. Be concise.** Below is the chosen response. </LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>

<LM_INPUT> It looks like the website you're trying to access may have disabled the default shortcut for opening developer tools in Chrome. You can try the following alternative methods:

1. Right-click anywhere on the webpage and select "Inspect" from the context menu.
2. Open the Chrome menu by clicking on the three dots in the upper right corner, then select "More tools" and then "Developer tools."
3. You can also use the shortcut Ctrl + Shift + J (or Cmd + Opt + J on Mac) to open the console, which will open the developer tools with the console tab active.

If none of these methods work, it's possible that the website is intentionally blocking developer tools from being opened. In this case, you may need to contact the website owner or find an alternative way to view the page source code. </LM_INPUT>

<LM_OUTPUT> **Chosen Response**:
It seems that the issue might be related to the specific website https://mnsw.pro/, as the developer tools shortcut (Ctrl + Shift + I) isn't working correctly there. You can try using an alternative method to open the developer tools:

1. Right-click on the webpage and select "Inspect" from the context menu.
2. Alternatively, you can use the shortcut Ctrl + Shift + J (or Cmd + Opt + J on a Mac) to open the console, which will also open the developer tools.

If these methods don't work, the website might have disabled the default developer tools shortcut. In this case, you can contact the website owner or use a different browser to access the website. </LM_OUTPUT>

<OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>Your goal is to give feedback and criticism to the variable given the above evaluation output. Our only goal is to improve the above metric, and nothing else. </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>

We are interested in giving feedback to the a chosen response to a user query for this conversation. Specifically, give feedback to the following span of text:

<VARIABLE> It looks like the website you're trying to access may (...) find an alternative way to view the page source code. </VARIABLE>

Given the above history, describe how the a chosen response to a user query could be improved to improve the <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>. Be very creative, critical, and intelligent.

Since language models have the tendency to provide generic solutions instead of focusing on the specific issue, the feedback should emphasize the unique aspects of the problem related to the given website. The response could be improved by considering the following suggestions:

1. Provide a more detailed explanation of the website's behavior: "It appears that the developer tools shortcut (Ctrl + Shift + I) is not working on the specific website https://mnsw.pro/. This could be due to the website's settings, which may have disabled the default shortcut for opening developer tools."

2. Suggest a more specific alternative method: "Instead of using the default shortcut, you can try using the following more specific method to open the developer tools on this specific website:

   - Right-click on the webpage and select 'Inspect' from the context menu.
   - Alternatively, you can use the shortcut Ctrl + Shift + J (or Cmd + Opt + J on a Mac) to open the console, which will also open the developer tools.

   If these methods don't work, it's possible that the website has disabled the default developer tools shortcut. In this case, you may want to contact the website owner or use a different browser to access the website."

By focusing on the unique aspects of the problem and providing more specific solutions, the response can better address the user's query and improve the overall quality of the chosen response.
